question_set.question: How do calories vary within and across beverage categories, and what role do sugar-related encodings play if they are visible?

answer.value: With x = Beverage_category and y = Calories (color still Beverage_category), each category forms a vertical band of points: within category, calories spread widely (e.g. Frappuccino® Blended Coffee and Signature Espresso Drinks span from roughly ~100–500 kcal in the data; Coffee stays ~3–5). Across categories, Coffee is uniformly low-calorie; Smoothies and Frappuccino® families sit highest on average. Sugar (g) is no longer on an axis after the encoding change; it remains available in tooltips for spot checks but does not drive x/y position in this final view.

key_insights: Within-category calorie dispersion is large for blended and signature drink categories; Coffee is a tight low band.
Cross-category ordering: blended/smoothie-style categories sit highest on the calorie axis; coffee lowest.

reasoning_trace.rationale: Remap x to Beverage_category so category-level and within-category calorie patterns can be read from the scatter.
